title: Released Windows updater locks its own console launcher
signatures: failed to remove file[^\r\n]*Scripts[/\\]hermes\.exe[^\r\n]*Access is denied\. \(os error 5\)
explanation: The March/April Windows updater is already running from hermes.exe when uv tries to replace it. Windows refuses the locked launcher. The update target cannot change that loaded code; re-running the installer is a separate recovery route.

title: July script installs offer a manual update instead of an app hand-off
errors: ^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: app driven via captured hermes desktop spec; update completed$
^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: GUI driver clicked Update now and the app quit for hand-off$
signatures: \[updates\] no staged updater; surfacing manual `hermes update` for CLI install at
explanation: The July Windows app has no staged updater after a script install. Its Update button explicitly returns manual: hermes update without starting a hand-off. Desktop-installer installs are not covered by this exception.

title: Pre-PM release trees cannot satisfy the published Hermes-Setup.exe (pm/lock.json absent)
signatures: bootstrap FAILED stage=Some\("venv"\) error=Cannot find path '[^']*pm[\\/]+lock\.json' because it does not exist
explanation: The published Hermes-Setup.exe bootstrap is pm-era: it drives the vendored package manager against the checkout it lands, and pre-pm release trees (v2026.9.24 and earlier) do not ship pm/lock.json, so the venv stage fails before any update runs. The Setup.exe comes from the release asset server, so the update target cannot repair it; the class resolves when a pm-bearing release is adopted.

title: Pre-PM release trees cannot satisfy the published Hermes-Setup.dmg (pm install fails at python-deps)
errors: ^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: dmg bootstrap exited [1-9][0-9]*; transcript above$
signatures: bootstrap FAILED stage=Some\("python-deps"\) error=pm install failed
explanation: The published Hermes-Setup.dmg bootstrap is pm-era: its python-deps stage runs the vendored package manager, which cannot install pre-pm release trees (v2026.9.24 and earlier ship no pm/lock.json). The dmg comes from the release asset server, so the update target cannot repair it; the class resolves when a pm-bearing release is adopted.

title: Pre-PM desktop app replaces itself during first launch, before Playwright's inspection pipe settles
errors: ^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: app-driven update exited [1-9][0-9]*; transcript above$
explanation: The pre-pm desktop app's first non-metadata startup may replace the packaged app and relaunch itself (bundle swap / update hand-off), which tears down the debugging port Playwright had just connected to: the process stays alive and prints its install stamp, but the electron.launch handshake never completes. Driving this reliably needs the launcher to settle the source runtime BEFORE attaching and isolate the update-window user data — a post-v2026.9.24 driver/product series this tree does not carry. Resolves at the next adoption.

title: Pre-PM June desktop builds ship a renderer layout the current driver contract rejects
errors: ^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: read-only verification failed (?:at OLD|after install); no repair was attempted$
^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: read-only verification failed after install$
^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: post-install-(?:gui|script-desktop) -- read-only install verification \(no repair\)$
signatures: RuntimeError: desktop packaged renderer is missing or incomplete
explanation: The June tree's desktop packaging emits its renderer without the app.asar.unpacked/dist/index.html product the current read-only source contract requires (source_driver.py verify_products), so every +desktop leg that installs v2026.6.5 fails read-only verification with the same deterministic signature before any update runs. On windows the same failure surfaces through Test-HermesRuns' read-only install assertion with a post-install-gui / post-install-script-desktop wrapper (fix-queue item 339, run 39368643437). The installed tree cannot repair its own historical packaging; the class resolves when a release with the current layout is the OLD sample.
